[LGRA.10.3.2] The grammar accepts any `kwarg | flag` sequence after the
action head; per-action validity is enforced at compile
time by the action's contract, which is [LGRA.10.3.3].

The split is one of **phase**, not of expressive power. A grammar applied
before name resolution must accept any `kwarg | flag` sequence, because "a
kwarg name must be a slot of the schema this action names" depends on which
schema that name resolves to, and at that point it has not. Once the name is
resolved the dependency is gone: the admissible set is fixed, and
[LGRA.10.3.3] closes the surface as a grammar over it. [LGRA.10.3.3] is where
every verb's contract lives.

So the contract is not a retreat from a grammar to a prose list. It is a
grammar, applied at the phase where its schema-dependent nonterminal has a
value: an ordinary attribute grammar, not a context-sensitive one.
